title: hosting.com Review 2026: Prices, Renewal Costs, Speed Tests and AI Tools
excerpt: hosting.com has some of the lowest first-year prices and some of the highest renewals. Here is the three-year cost, how it tested, and who should skip it.

meta._yoast_wpseo_title: hosting.com Review 2026: Prices, Renewals, Speed, AI
meta._yoast_wpseo_metadesc: hosting.com review for 2026: sale and renewal prices, three-year cost, speed tests from HostingAdvice, CNET and Website Planet, AI tools, pros and cons.
meta.rl_answer: hosting.com, the new name of A2 Hosting, has fast servers and very low first-year prices from $1.49 a month. Renewals are about 9.4 times higher on Starter, and CNET does not recommend it for beginners.
meta.rl_faqs:
Is hosting.com good? | It has fast servers and low first-year prices. CNET recommends it only for experienced users, and renewal prices are high.
Is hosting.com the same as A2 Hosting? | Yes. A2 Hosting said on its own blog in April 2025 that it was now hosting.com.
How much does hosting.com cost? | Starter is $1.49 a month on a 12-month plan and renews at $13.99 a month. Pro is $3.49 and Max is $5.99 on sale.
Is hosting.com good for beginners? | CNET says no and calls setup overly complicated. HostingAdvice found live chat fast, so test support early.
How fast is hosting.com? | HostingAdvice measured a Largest Contentful Paint of 579 ms on the cheap plan and an A grade on WordPress hosting.
Does hosting.com have hidden fees? | We found none. The cost to plan for is the high renewal price.
Does hosting.com have a money-back guarantee? | Yes. hosting.com lists a 30-day money-back guarantee.
Does hosting.com have AI features? | Yes. It lists Orbi, an AI website builder, an MCP server and a Claude Skills Pack. We did not test them.
Can hosting.com handle high-traffic websites? | Performance Plus load balancing is listed on all plans. For a busy site, test during the refund window or compare Cloudways and Kinsta.
Does hosting.com offer free migration? | Yes. The Black Friday page lists free migration and a free domain for 1 year.
Is hosting.com better than Hostinger? | Its first-year price is lower. Hostinger's sale price lasts 48 months and its renewal is lower.
Who should avoid hosting.com? | Beginners, people who want a low price for years and anyone who wants a simple setup.

meta.rl_takeaways:
Starter is $1.49 a month on a 12-month plan and renews at $13.99.
Over three years, Starter averages $9.82 a month.
HostingAdvice measured a 579 ms Largest Contentful Paint.
CNET recommends hosting.com only for experienced website owners.
meta.rl_r_verdict: hosting.com is a good deal for the first year and an expensive one after that. Servers are fast and the AI tools are the most complete we found, but CNET and Website Planet both flag weak support and a harder setup.
meta.rl_r_buy:
You want the lowest first-year bill and free migration.
You are comfortable with hosting tools and want AI features included.
You plan to move or re-shop after the first term.
meta.rl_r_skip:
You are new to hosting and want a simple setup.
You want a low price for several years.
You rely on support knowing the product.
meta.rl_r_pros:
Very low sale prices from $1.49 a month.
Fast servers in independent tests.
Free migration and a free domain for 1 year.
A wide set of AI tools.
A 30-day money-back guarantee.
meta.rl_r_cons:
Renewal is about 9.4 times the sale price on Starter.
CNET calls setup overly complicated and support poor.
The sale price needs a 12-month plan.
meta.rl_r_best: People who want the lowest first-year bill and AI tools
meta.rl_r_method:
Pricing and terms | hosting.com's plan and Black Friday pages, read on 15 November 2026: sale prices, renewal prices, free items and the guarantee
Independent tests | HostingAdvice (two weeks, GTmetrix and live chat), CNET (the reviewer bought a plan and tracked speed, uptime and support) and Website Planet (shared and WordPress plans)
Competitor reviews | The top-ranking hosting.com and A2 Hosting reviews read, and their questions compared
Our calculations | The three-year cost table is our own arithmetic from hosting.com's prices
When sources disagree | We show both numbers. For prices we use hosting.com's own page
Freshness | Prices and offers are read again before this page goes live
What we did not do | We did not run our own speed or uptime test
